comprehension: Phase: yes, the round bug top left (Round one, The booth, The reveal) and full-screen title calls name it. Show type: partly. 'Compatibility Mode' does not say dating; the hearts, 'Vesper's type' and 'Vesper picks Frost' get there, but nothing on screen says it is bots or that viewers bet; there are no odds, stakes or a 'bet now' cue anywhere. Who is winning: unclear. The pips under suitors (09) mix hearts, raindrops and a raincloud with no key, the dimmed Sir Quill tag shows a cut but is subtle, and the hand ('Bad puns', '?', '?', 'The Ex') does not explain that suitors are matched against hidden turn-ons and a dealbreaker. 'The Ex' tab has no context at all once the twist card is gone. A newcomer would know it is a show with rounds and a picker, not who leads.
biggestGap: The top-right type hand is the least professional area and it is on screen in every studio shot: by the reveal it is a six-piece pile (three mini cards, 'The Ex' tab wedged under a seam, the type label overlapping the last card, and the big card 10-25 px below repeating the same words), whereas Animal Crossing and Monster Prom never let more than one text element compete in a zone. Rebuild it as one clean row with a fixed 12 px gap and the label as a plate at the row's left end (like the name tags), move 'The Ex' out to sit beside the round bug as a rule badge, and hide the mini hand entirely while the big card is up so there is at least 40 px of air and no duplicated text.
protect: The subtitle bar's scale and type: ~38 px cream on ink navy, two lines, hand-cut edge, about 78% frame width, bottom anchored; it reads instantly at 960x540 and matches Monster Prom and Animal Crossing proportions.

Tilted speaker plates in each suitor's accent colour overlapping the bar's top-left corner (Dash, Vesper, 'Sir Quill, earlier', 'Tilly, earlier'), with the bar keyline switching to mint for a turn-on and coral for a dealbreaker; this is the Animal Crossing 'Punchy' tag done right and gives the replay its own voice.
09's cut treatment: Sir Quill's tag drops to his own colour, dimmed, while the others stay lit; it is the Take Me Out lights-out grammar applied to type and reads without a word.
